Definition: to open, i.e. be (causatively, make) roomy; usually figuratively (in a mental or moral sense) to be (causatively, make) simple or (in a sinister way) delude
BiblicalUsage: Pathah means to open, to make roomy, and figuratively to entice or deceive. Moses warns in Deuteronomy 11:16 that the heart must not be deceived and turn aside to serve other gods. A lying spirit offers to entice Ahab in 1 Kings 22:20, and the Lord says, thou shalt persuade him, in 1 Kings 22:22. The same enticing stands in 2 Chronicles 18:20, where the spirit stands before the Lord and says, I will entice him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a deceived heart is an opened door, and the lying spirit that enticed Ahab entered through a king who wanted to hear what he wanted. That is why I hold that the warning in Deuteronomy is for me: guard the heart, or it will be opened by the wrong voice.
